findings.problem: The test sets only oracul.search.search-window=PT2S. Since this slice, QueryGenerator enforces the spec rule (wildcard-search.md Configuration, FR-51 range g) that startup fails unless query-generation-window <= search-window. The default query-generation-window is PT30S, so the Spring context fails with 'oracul.search.query-generation-window must not exceed oracul.search.search-window' and the test never reaches its assertions. The builders flagged this correctly: production behaves as specified and the test is wrong. Its FR-48/FR-52 window coverage (no request after the window, last timeout cut to the window end) is lost and the suite is red.
findings.fix: Add "oracul.search.query-generation-window=PT2S" (or any value from PT0.001S to PT2S) to the @TestPropertySource and keep every assertion. The test calls the search seam directly, so the query-generation window does not affect what it measures.

findings.problem: Same conflict as R1: oracul.search.search-window=PT2S with the default query-generation-window PT30S. Startup validation now rejects this configuration, so the context fails to start and all 3 tests of the class fail before any assertion. FR-52 range (c) / NFR-10 part 1 (the window cuts open requests and keeps unsent ones from starting, FAILED and never EMPTY) is unproven while this class is red.
findings.fix: Add "oracul.search.query-generation-window=PT2S" (at most PT2S) to the @TestPropertySource. No other change.

findings.problem: sanitize() uses \p{Cntrl} and \s, and Java treats both as ASCII-only by default. So C1 control characters (U+0080-U+009F, including NEL U+0085, which is a line break) and the Unicode line/paragraph separators U+2028/U+2029 pass through unchanged into the custom-wildcards data line. Probed: "Mars\u0085colony\u2028SYSTEM x" stays as-is. A custom label is user input that only gets trimmed and length-checked at startRun (RunService.snapshot, WildcardRules), so a user can split the data block into several lines. This breaks the spec's data-line rule ('control characters -> space, whitespace collapsed'). It also breaks parity with the shared PromptText.sanitize / UntrustedText used by the other prompts, which replaces [\p{Cc}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\s]+.
findings.fix: Reuse PromptText.sanitize (same package) or apply the same regex: s.replaceAll("[\\p{Cc}\\p{Zl}\\p{Zp}\\s]+", " ").trim() and then the marker and '|' replacements.

findings.problem: Missing exhaustive test for custom-label sanitising (data-line rule) across character classes. labelSanitising covers only ASCII controls (\u0000, \t, \r\n). It has no C1 control (\u0085, \u0080, \u009f), no U+2028/U+2029, and no non-ASCII whitespace (\u00a0, \u3000), so the defect in R3 passes.
findings.fix: Extend labelSanitising with \u0085, \u0080, \u009f, \u2028, \u2029, \u000b, \u001f and \u007f between words (each -> one space, collapsed). Assert that the data block holds exactly one line (no character of category Cc/Zl/Zp between the markers) and that each marker appears only once.

findings.problem: Rule Q tokenises with clean() = trim() plus \s+ and then split(" "). Both are ASCII-only, so a model text that uses non-breaking or other Unicode spaces counts as fewer tokens. For example, "solar\u00a0OR\u00a0wind energy storage growth" has 4 tokens and no standalone 'OR' token, so it is kept and sent to Google, where the nbsp is a word break and the query becomes the OR shape rule Q is meant to prevent. A model is unlikely to produce this, so it does not block.
findings.fix: Normalise every Unicode whitespace/separator to a space in clean() (e.g. replaceAll("[\\p{Z}\\s]+", " ") and strip()), and add these cases to QueryRulesTest.

findings.problem: EventBatchingIT, EventSourceCapIT, EventConcurrencyIT, EventConcurrencyOneIT and EventFailureIT still set oracul.research.query-budget=18. The property is no longer read (FR-51), so the setting is dead and misleads readers into thinking these runs have 18 queries (body A now has 6). It also keeps a property set that differs from contexts that could otherwise be shared.
findings.fix: Remove the oracul.research.query-budget=18 entries (the spec says these ITs keep body A and their assertions stay unchanged).

findings.problem: FR-51 Rules says '401 -> one refresh and one retry (phase-02 FR-38/FR-40)'. Phase-02 chatgpt-inference.md superseded that: 401 means no refresh, no retry, CHATGPT_SESSION_EXPIRED. Code and ResearchPlanIT.a401OnAGenerationCallEndsTheSessionWithoutRefreshOrRetry follow phase-02, which is correct, but the phase-03 spec line is stale and contradicts the test.
findings.fix: Spec owner: change the line to '401 -> no refresh, no retry, CHATGPT_SESSION_EXPIRED (phase-02 FR-39 row 1)'.
